9. Uttarikaraṇīyapañha 9. Question on What Remains to Be Done

“Bhante nāgasena, tumhe bhaṇatha—“Venerable Nāgasena, you say: ‘yaṁ kiñci karaṇīyaṁ tathāgatassa, sabbaṁ taṁ bodhiyāyeva mūle pariniṭṭhitaṁ, natthi tathāgatassa uttariṁ karaṇīyaṁ, katassa vā paticayo’ti, idañca temāsaṁ paṭisallānaṁ dissati. ‘Whatever had to be done by the Tathāgata, all of that was completed at the very foot of the Bodhi tree. There is nothing further for the Tathāgata to do, nor any accumulation of what has been done.’ And yet this three-month seclusion is observed. Yadi, bhante nāgasena, yaṁ kiñci karaṇīyaṁ tathāgatassa, sabbaṁ taṁ bodhiyāyeva mūle pariniṭṭhitaṁ, natthi tathāgatassa uttariṁ karaṇīyaṁ, katassa vā paticayo, tena hi ‘temāsaṁ paṭisallīno’ti yaṁ vacanaṁ, taṁ micchā. If, Venerable Nāgasena, whatever had to be done by the Tathāgata was all completed at the foot of the Bodhi tree, with nothing further to do and no accumulation of what is done, then the statement that ‘he was in seclusion for three months’ is false. Yadi temāsaṁ paṭisallīno, tena hi ‘yaṁ kiñci karaṇīyaṁ, tathāgatassa, sabbaṁ taṁ bodhiyāyeva mūle pariniṭṭhitan’ti tampi vacanaṁ micchā. If he was in seclusion for three months, then the statement that ‘whatever had to be done by the Tathāgata was all completed at the foot of the Bodhi tree’ is also false. Natthi katakaraṇīyassa paṭisallānaṁ, sakaraṇīyasseva paṭisallānaṁ yathā nāma byādhitasseva bhesajjena karaṇīyaṁ hoti, abyādhitassa kiṁ bhesajjena. For one who has done what was to be done, there is no seclusion. Seclusion belongs only to one who still has something to do. Just as only one who is sick has need of medicine (what use is medicine to one who is not sick?), Chātasseva bhojanena karaṇīyaṁ hoti, achātassa kiṁ bhojanena. and only one who is hungry has need of food (what use is food to one who is not hungry?), Evameva kho, bhante nāgasena, natthi katakaraṇīyassa paṭisallānaṁ, sakaraṇīyasseva paṭisallānaṁ. in the same way, Venerable Nāgasena, there is no seclusion for one who has done what was to be done; seclusion is only for one who still has something to do. Ayampi ubhato koṭiko pañho tavānuppatto, so tayā nibbāhitabbo”ti. This two-horned dilemma has now come to you, and it must be resolved by you.”

“Yaṁ kiñci, mahārāja, karaṇīyaṁ tathāgatassa, sabbaṁ taṁ bodhiyāyeva mūle pariniṭṭhitaṁ, natthi tathāgatassa uttariṁ karaṇīyaṁ, katassa vā paticayo, bhagavā ca temāsaṁ paṭisallīno, paṭisallānaṁ kho, mahārāja, bahuguṇaṁ, sabbepi tathāgatā paṭisallīyitvā sabbaññutaṁ pattā, taṁ te sukataguṇamanussarantā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. “Your majesty, whatever had to be done by the Tathāgata was all completed at the very foot of the Bodhi tree. There is nothing further for the Tathāgata to do, nor any accumulation of what has been done. And the Blessed One was in seclusion for three months. Seclusion, your majesty, has many benefits. All the Tathāgatas attained omniscience after being in seclusion, and, remembering that well-done benefit, they resort to seclusion. Yathā, mahārāja, puriso rañño santikā laddhavaro paṭiladdhabhogo taṁ sukataguṇamanussaranto aparāparaṁ rañño upaṭṭhānaṁ eti; Just as, your majesty, a man who has received a boon from the king and obtained wealth, remembering that good deed, keeps going back to attend upon the king, evameva kho, mahārāja, sabbepi tathāgatā paṭisallīyitvā sabbaññutaṁ pattā, taṁ te sukataguṇamanussarantā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. in the same way all the Tathāgatas, having attained omniscience through seclusion, resort to seclusion remembering its benefit.

Yathā vā pana, mahārāja, puriso āturo dukkhito bāḷhagilāno bhisakkamupasevitvā sotthimanuppatto taṁ sukataguṇamanussaranto aparāparaṁ bhisakkamupasevati; Or again, your majesty, just as a man who was ill, suffering, and gravely sick, and who attained safety by resorting to a physician, keeps going back to the physician remembering that benefit, evameva kho, mahārāja, sabbepi tathāgatā paṭisallīyitvā sabbaññutaṁ pattā, taṁ te sukataguṇamanussarantā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. in the same way all the Tathāgatas, having attained omniscience through seclusion, resort to seclusion remembering its benefit.

Aṭṭhavīsati kho panime, mahārāja, paṭisallānaguṇā, ye guṇe samanussarantā tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. There are, your majesty, twenty-eight qualities of seclusion, and it is in remembrance of these that the Tathāgatas resort to it. Katame aṭṭhavīsati? Which twenty-eight? Idha, mahārāja, paṭisallānaṁ paṭisallīyamānaṁ attānaṁ rakkhati, āyuṁ vaḍḍheti, balaṁ deti, vajjaṁ pidahati, ayasamapaneti, yasamupaneti, aratiṁ vinodeti, ratimupadahati, bhayamapaneti, vesārajjaṁ karoti, kosajjamapaneti, vīriyamabhijaneti, rāgamapaneti, dosamapaneti, mohamapaneti, mānaṁ nihanti, vitakkaṁ bhañjati, cittaṁ ekaggaṁ karoti, mānasaṁ snehayati, hāsaṁ janeti, garukaṁ karoti, lābhamuppādayati, namassiyaṁ karoti, pītiṁ pāpeti, pāmojjaṁ karoti, saṅkhārānaṁ sabhāvaṁ dassayati, bhavappaṭisandhiṁ ugghāṭeti, sabbasāmaññaṁ deti. Here, your majesty, seclusion, when practiced, protects oneself, increases life, gives strength, covers over faults, removes disrepute, brings good repute, dispels discontent, brings delight, removes fear, produces confidence, removes laziness, arouses energy, removes lust, removes hatred, removes delusion, destroys conceit, shatters (wandering) thoughts, makes the mind one-pointed, softens the heart, produces gladness, makes one weighty (dignified), brings gain, makes one worthy of homage, leads to joy, produces gladdening delight, shows the true nature of formations, opens up (breaks) rebirth-linking in existence, gives everything that belongs to the ascetic life. Ime kho, mahārāja, aṭṭhavīsati paṭisallānaguṇā, ye guṇe samanussarantā tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. These, your majesty, are the twenty-eight qualities of seclusion, and remembering them the Tathāgatas resort to it.

Api ca kho, mahārāja, tathāgatā santaṁ sukhaṁ samāpattiratiṁ anubhavitukāmā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti pariyositasaṅkappā. Moreover, your majesty, the Tathāgatas, whose resolves are fulfilled, resort to seclusion wishing to experience peaceful happiness and the delight of attainments. Catūhi kho, mahārāja, kāraṇehi tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. The Tathāgatas resort to seclusion for four reasons. Katamehi catūhi? Which four? Vihāraphāsutāyapi, mahārāja, tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti, anavajjaguṇabahulatāyapi tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti, asesaariyavīthitopi tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti, sabbabuddhānaṁ thutathomitavaṇṇitapasatthatopi tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. The Tathāgatas resort to seclusion for a comfortable dwelling; for its abundance of blameless qualities; because it belongs to the entire noble way; and because it is praised, extolled, described, and commended by all the Buddhas. Imehi kho, mahārāja, catūhi kāraṇehi tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti. For these four reasons, your majesty, the Tathāgatas resort to seclusion. Iti kho, mahārāja, tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevanti na sakaraṇīyatāya, na katassa vā paticayāya, atha kho guṇavisesadassāvitāya tathāgatā paṭisallānaṁ sevantī”ti. Thus, your majesty, the Tathāgatas resort to seclusion not because they still have something to do, nor for the accumulation of what has been done, but because they see its special excellence.” “Sādhu, bhante nāgasena, evametaṁ tathā sampaṭicchāmī”ti. “Very good, Venerable Nāgasena. I accept it as you say.”

Uttarikaraṇīyapañho navamo. Question on What Remains to Be Done ninth
